title: The Last Day of Rome: The Fall of Constantinople, 1453

style.prefix: Photorealistic cinematic film still from a high-budget historical documentary reconstruction, shot on ARRI Alexa with anamorphic lenses, natural film grain, realistic skin and fabric texture, controlled highlights, detailed shadows
style.suffix: historically accurate mid-15th-century details, no text, no captions, no watermark, no modern objects, no fantasy elements
style.negative: cartoon, illustration, painting, CGI look, oversaturated, HDR, plastic skin, anime, text, logo, watermark, modern buildings, minarets on Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque, Topkapi Palace, Galata Bridge, electric lights, gore

grades.gold: warm golden-hour sunlight, amber and honey tones, soft atmospheric haze over the water
grades.candle: warm candlelight and oil lamps, deep shadows, gold mosaic glints, incense haze
grades.steel: overcast cold daylight, desaturated steel-blue and stone-grey palette, drifting gunpowder smoke
grades.night: night, moonlight blue with orange firelight and torches, smoke catching the light
grades.dawn: pre-dawn cold blue light turning to pale grey, burning fires on the horizon, heavy smoke
grades.ash: muted, low-contrast, ash-grey and faded ochre, quiet aftermath light

refs.constantine: Emperor Constantine XI Palaiologos, a man of 48 with a lean weathered face, dark beard flecked with grey, tired dignified eyes; wears a deep crimson-purple cloak over steel lamellar and mail armour, purple-red imperial boots, a simple gold circlet only in ceremonial scenes
refs.mehmed: Sultan Mehmed II at 21, slim, sharp aquiline nose, thin dark moustache and short young beard, intense intelligent eyes; large white wrapped turban, red and gold silk kaftan with long sleeves, jewelled dagger at the sash
refs.giustiniani: Giovanni Giustiniani Longo, a Genoese soldier in his forties, short dark beard, hard practical face; full polished Italian plate armour of the 1450s, red Genoese cross sash, open-faced sallet helmet
refs.orban: Orban, a Hungarian cannon founder in his forties, broad shoulders, heavy moustache, soot-stained face, leather apron over a plain wool tunic
refs.notaras: Loukas Notaras, an elderly Byzantine grand duke, white beard, tall domed brimmed hat (skiadion), heavy brocade robes in blue and gold
refs.sphrantzes: George Sphrantzes, a Byzantine courtier in his fifties, neat greying beard, plain dark wool robes, a scribe's ink-stained fingers
refs.barbaro: Nicolo Barbaro, a Venetian ship's doctor in his thirties, clean-shaven, black physician's robe and cap
refs.halil: Candarli Halil Pasha, the elderly Ottoman grand vizier, grey beard, tall white turban, sober dark green kaftan
refs.janissaries: Ottoman janissaries in tall white felt bork caps with a folded flap at the back, long robes tucked into sashes, composite bows, some with early matchlock handguns
refs.azaps: Ottoman irregular troops and volunteers, mixed simple clothing, wicker shields, spears and ladders
refs.defenders: Byzantine and Italian defenders in mixed mail, brigandines and kettle helmets, crossbows, pavise shields, a few early handguns
refs.walls: the Theodosian land walls of Constantinople: a wide dry moat, a lower outer wall and a massive inner wall with tall mostly square towers and a few octagonal ones, built of pale limestone blocks with horizontal bands of red brick, weathered and patched by a thousand years, clean grassy ground with no debris
refs.lycus: the Mesoteichion, the stretch of the land walls where the Lycus valley dips, near the Gate of St Romanus, the weakest point of the walls
refs.city1453: Constantinople in 1453: a shrunken city of scattered neighbourhoods, orchards, fields and ruined churches inside vast old walls, the great dome of Hagia Sophia with heavy buttresses and no minarets
refs.hagia: Hagia Sophia in 1453 before any minarets: a vast central dome on buttressed walls; inside, gold mosaics, marble columns, a ring of windows under the dome flooding light
refs.horn: the Golden Horn, a long sheltered harbour between Constantinople and the walled Genoese town of Galata with its tall stone tower on the hill
refs.chain: a massive iron chain across the mouth of the Golden Horn, held up on wooden log floats, with Venetian and Genoese ships anchored behind it
refs.rumeli: Rumeli Hisari, a new Ottoman fortress of grey stone with three great towers climbing a steep hillside on the European shore of the narrowest point of the Bosphorus
refs.camp: the Ottoman siege camp: a sea of red, white and green tents, banners, horses, camels, smoke from cooking fires, the sultan's large red pavilion
refs.bombard: Orban's giant bronze bombard, a barrel about eight metres long, lying on a heavy timber cradle, with huge round stone balls stacked beside it
